title: Metta Sutta 1
speaker: Nomon Tim Burnett
summary: Nomon Tim Burnett takes up the Metta Sutta, the loving-kindness text chanted at the Monday, Wednesday, and Friday noon services, as the first session of a four-week class. Nomon traces how the sutta reached the sangha through the Pali canon and Norman Fischer, then compares the chanted English with Thanissaro Bhikkhu's more literal translation. The comparison turns on the step-by-step early teachings versus Zen's "already complete" view, and on words like "easy to correct" and "having few duties" that the chanted version drops. Nomon plays a Sri Lankan chanting of the verses, then closes with the sutta's test of doing nothing the wise would reprove, a news story of four monks arrested in Yangon for reciting the sutta, and small-group sharing in threes.
topics: Buddhist teachings on virtue and morality
